questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 55°. What is the alternate angle on the other line?
questions.why: Alternate angles between parallel lines are always equal, so the answer is 55°. 125° would be the co-interior angle instead.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Magna Carta 1215 was mainly agreed to limit the power of whom?
questions.why: Magna Carta forced King John to accept limits on royal power, making him subject to the law like everyone else.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A quadrilateral has two pairs of parallel sides and all four sides equal, but no right angles. What is the most specific name for this shape?
questions.why: A rhombus has four equal sides and two pairs of parallel sides but does not need right angles. A square needs right angles too, a kite has no parallel sides, and a rectangle needs right angles but not equal sides.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: In which year did the First Crusade set out to capture Jerusalem?
questions.why: The First Crusade began in 1096, launched after Pope Urban II called for a campaign to take Jerusalem.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: What best describes a 'trigger' cause of a historical event?
questions.why: A trigger cause is the short-term event that sets things off immediately, unlike long-term causes which build up over years.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.why: Globalisation refers to countries becoming more linked through trade, travel, and communication, not more isolated.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In which Italian city is Romeo and Juliet set?
questions.why: Shakespeare set Romeo and Juliet in Verona, home to the feuding Montague and Capulet families.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A student tests whether the type of fertiliser affects plant height, using the same pot size and water amount for every plant. What is the controlled variable here?
questions.why: The controlled variables are the things kept the same on purpose, like pot size and water, so only the fertiliser's effect is tested.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: What technique does Shakespeare use when Romeo and Juliet speak in a shared sonnet at their first meeting?
questions.why: Romeo and Juliet's first exchange forms a shared sonnet, showing their instant connection through matching poetic structure.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of asexual reproduction for many simple organisms?
questions.why: Asexual reproduction lets organisms multiply rapidly since only one parent is needed, though offspring are genetically identical.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 83°. What is the co-interior angle on the other line?
questions.why: Co-interior angles add up to 180°, so 180° minus 83° gives 97°. They are not equal like alternate angles.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Your classmate says: 'In an experiment testing whether room temperature affects how fast ice melts, the melting time is the independent variable because it's what changes the most.' Using an example of your own (not sleep, sunlight, fertiliser, water temperature, or soil type), explain what actually makes a variable independent, dependent, or controlled, and correct your classmate's mistake.
